verdicts.title: Angels' Den 2026
verdicts.quote: If you would like information on how to apply for Angels' Den 2026, please email rsvp@theclarefoundation.org.
verdicts.for_paul: An annual event in its fourth year; the 2026 round has closed, the event is on 9 September, and the page names no 2027 date. Keep the row waiting for next year's page, or reject it as historic and re-add a fresh one?

verdicts.title: Apply for Investment (Fund Manager Route)
verdicts.quote: We invest in fund managers who provide finance or other support to social enterprises and charities, we do not invest directly the organisations themselves.
verdicts.for_paul: Better Society Capital lends to fund managers, not to charities. Nothing here for a fundraiser to apply to.

verdicts.title: Ashoka Fellowship
verdicts.for_paul: HTTP 403 behind a Cloudflare interstitial, so the page could not be read today. The row's stored brief says fellows are identified and nominated rather than applying directly; if that holds it is a reject, but it needs a browser read to confirm.

verdicts.title: B&Q Foundation Community Grants
verdicts.quote: Find out more about our charity partnerships and how we support our local communities.
verdicts.for_paul: Duplicate of the live row cb9780e6, B&Q Foundation Home Improvement & Home-Starter Kits Funds, which points at bqfoundation.org.uk. This row points at the diy.com retail site, where the foundation gets one line and no application route.

verdicts.title: Barclays 100x100 UK Community Relief Programme
verdicts.quote: Page not found - GrantFinder
verdicts.for_paul: A COVID-19 relief programme from 2020. apply_url was never Barclays' own page but an Idox GrantFinder listing, which now returns 404, so there is nothing to relink to either.

verdicts.title: Baring Foundation — International Development Programme
verdicts.quote: Please note that applications to the International Development Programme are always by invitation only.
verdicts.for_paul: Invitation only, in the foundation's own words and without qualification. The Baring Foundation's other programmes may be worth carrying separately; this one has no route in.

verdicts.title: Big Society Capital Social Investment Wholesale Funding
verdicts.quote: We invest in fund managers who provide finance or other support to social enterprises and charities, we do not invest directly the organisations themselves.
verdicts.for_paul: The same wholesaler as row 2 and the same reason: it invests in fund managers, not in charities. apply_url here is the homepage, so the sentence is quoted from the apply-for-investment page on the same site. Also a near-duplicate of row 2, though neither is live.

verdicts.title: Brighton & Hove — Fairness Fund for Communities 2025/26
verdicts.quote: The Fairness Fund is now closed to applications.
verdicts.for_paul: The 2025/26 round has closed and the page gives no 2026/27 date. The council runs it annually and the row is year-stamped in its title, so the choice is between holding this row for next year's page and rejecting it in favour of a fresh row when the next round opens.

verdicts.title: Charities and Social Enterprises Lending
verdicts.quote: Charities, social enterprises and community projects make up a large share of our customer base
verdicts.for_paul: Duplicate of the live row 6c5b16b7, Triodos Bank UK Business Loans, at triodos.co.uk/business-lending. Worth knowing before rejecting: this hidden row's URL is the more specific charities and social enterprises page, so relinking the live row to it and rejecting this one may be the better trade.

verdicts.title: Charity and Co-operative Lending Fund
verdicts.quote: For registered charities, co-operatives, credit unions and community-interest companies only.

verdicts.title: Charity Bank — Green Loans
verdicts.quote: We offer loans up to £7.5 million, with larger amounts available through partnerships with other social lenders.

verdicts.title: Charity Bank Loans
verdicts.quote: Charity Bank is a savings and loan bank with a mission to use money for good. We use money our savers entrust to us to make loans to UK charities, social enterprises and organisations with charitable purposes.
verdicts.for_paul: Duplicate of the live row 72739682, Charity Bank Loans for Social Purpose, at charitybank.org/loans. This row points at the bank's homepage and its amount_max of £3.25m matches nothing on it.

verdicts.title: CLA Charitable Trust
verdicts.quote: We are not accepting any further applications in 2026. We expect to re-open in December/January for our 2027 grant-making.

verdicts.title: Commonweal Housing — Call for New Ideas
verdicts.quote: Applications are open until Friday 16th October 2026.
verdicts.for_paul: Open until 16 October, which matches the row's deadline, and the fund is real. The row carries £5,000 to £10,000 and the page states no figure anywhere — it is in the downloadable Application Guide. Confirm the range from the guide or clear it, and this becomes a publish.

verdicts.title: Community Housing Fund
verdicts.quote: Organisations and groups who want to bid for revenue and/or capital funding should contact the Community-Led Housing London Hub to discuss their application.
verdicts.for_paul: Two problems. apply_url points at the GLA's funding-programmes index, where the fund is a bare link; its own page (quoted here) describes the route but gives no dates, no amounts and no exclusions, so it cannot carry a full brief. Its published allocations also stop at Q4 2024-25. Relink and confirm the programme is still running, or reject it as ended.

verdicts.title: Community Investment Enterprise Facility (CIEF)
verdicts.quote: We established the Community Investment Enterprise Facility (CIEF) in 2015 (in partnership with Social Investment Scotland) to provide CDFIs with the capital they need to meet demand
verdicts.for_paul: CIEF puts capital into CDFIs, which then lend to small businesses. The £25,000 to £250,000 on the row is what a CDFI lends on, not what this facility offers an applicant. Third Better Society Capital row in this pile with the same shape.

verdicts.title: CPCA Social Impact Investment Fund
verdicts.quote: Social impact workspace, next to Peterborough United FC stadium.
verdicts.for_paul: futurebusinesscentre.co.uk now redirects to alliaworkspace.co.uk, which sells flexible offices and meeting rooms. No trace of the CPCA fund anywhere on it.

verdicts.title: DCR Allen Charitable Trust
verdicts.quote: Total expenditure: £163,658
verdicts.for_paul: apply_url is a Charity Commission register entry rather than a funder page: it can say who may apply and never how to apply, so the row cannot carry a complete brief. The trust is real and spending £163,658 a year, and it has no website. Carry it as a funder a fundraiser can only write to, or reject it as unapproachable?

verdicts.title: Desk Space and Meeting Room Hire for Charities
verdicts.quote: Looking for desk space on an ad hoc basis with no ongoing commitment? Then we can offer you a hot desk for as little as £30 per day.
verdicts.for_paul: Priced workspace hire, not an in-kind offer: £120 a month for a fixed desk, £30 a day for a hot desk. The row carried it as in-kind with a £200 ceiling, which is a price rather than an award.

verdicts.title: Edward Gostling Foundation Grants
verdicts.quote: We have closed all our grant application programmes and instead have invited carefully chosen charities to work with us going forward as Legacy Partners.
verdicts.for_paul: All application programmes closed; the foundation now works only with invited Legacy Partners while it spends out.

verdicts.title: Employer-Supported Skilled Volunteering Programmes
verdicts.quote: Coaches and individuals meet virtually for up to six sessions over the course of several weeks.
verdicts.for_paul: The page is written for corporate members wanting to deploy their staff, and states no route for a charity to request support. Its apply_url is admin-pinned, so it cannot be relinked in this job. Probably a reject as a membership body, but the pin makes it yours.

verdicts.title: Energy Resilience Fund
verdicts.quote: Currently open? yes
verdicts.for_paul: Duplicate of the live row 6e6e8050, Energy Resilience Fund — Social Investment Business, whose £25,000 to £250,000 already matches the fund page. This hidden row points at goodfinance.org.uk, a third-party directory, and carries £60,000 to £15,000,000, which describes SIB's lending in general rather than this fund. Two smaller things while you are there: the live row's apply_url uses /fund/ where the page I read today is /funds/, and there is a second live SIB row (583f0378, Social Investment Business — Resilience Fund) pointing at the funding index.

verdicts.title: EY Foundation Programmes for Young People
verdicts.for_paul: ey.foundation did not answer on repeated attempts, so nothing could be read today. Needs a re-read before any verdict.

verdicts.title: Foundation East CDFI Loans
verdicts.quote: EE Pay By Mobile Casino UK: 2026's Premier Guide | Foundation East
verdicts.for_paul: The CDFI's domain has been taken over and now serves a gambling affiliate site under the charity's name, complete with casino bonus tables and an invented staff bio. Reject the row, and it may be worth checking whether anything else in the catalogue points at foundationeast.org.

verdicts.title: FSI Small Charity Training and Capacity Building Programme
verdicts.quote: Index of / Name Last Modified Size cgi-bin Proudly Served by LiteSpeed Web Server at thefsi.org Port 443
verdicts.for_paul: thefsi.org serves a bare Apache directory index with one cgi-bin folder last modified in 2023. The Foundation for Social Improvement's site is gone.

verdicts.title: Gatwick Foundation Fund (via SCF Main Grants)
verdicts.quote: The maximum grant available is £10,000 for exceptional projects, although many successful applications will be for less than this amount.
verdicts.for_paul: The fund is real, open and has been renamed the London Gatwick Community Fund; apply_url redirects to the new page. Seven of its fields are admin-pinned, including apply_url and a deadline of 5 June that has passed, so nothing can be tidied here. Sussex Main grants close on 11 September. Unpin and it is a publish.

verdicts.title: General Grants
verdicts.quote: Grants are made to registered charities.
verdicts.for_paul: apply_url is a Charity Commission register entry rather than a funder page: it can say who may apply and never how to apply, so the row cannot carry a complete brief. The Djanogly Foundation spends £330,942 a year and has no site of its own.

verdicts.title: Harford Charitable Trust
verdicts.quote: We are a small Family Trust making grants (maximum £2,000) to registered charities (not individuals).
verdicts.for_paul: The best of the four register rows: the entry states who may apply, a £2,000 ceiling and that individuals are excluded, which is three of the seven brief fields. It still cannot say how to apply, because a Charity Commission register entry rather than a funder page: it can say who may apply and never how to apply, so the row cannot carry a complete brief.

verdicts.title: Henry Smith Foundation — Career Ready
verdicts.quote: You can see which programmes are currently open below. If your work aligns with our priorities but funding isn't open right now, sign up to our mailing list to hear when programmes open.
verdicts.for_paul: Career Ready and Maternity Equity are both cards on this one page, and the page carries exactly one "Coming Soon" badge and one "Closed" badge. Which belongs to which does not survive a text read, and guessing would put a wrong status on one of them. Needs a browser look; the two rows should be decided together.

verdicts.title: Henry Smith Foundation — Maternity Equity
verdicts.quote: You can see which programmes are currently open below. If your work aligns with our priorities but funding isn't open right now, sign up to our mailing list to hear when programmes open.
verdicts.for_paul: Paired with the Career Ready row above and blocked the same way. This row already records "Listed as Coming Soon; no opening date published", which is a park only if a date appears; today the page still gives none.
